Trace its parsing delegation and cite the source.","response":"`pg_parse_query` performs **raw parsing only** — lexical and grammatical analysis of a SQL query string, returning a `List` of raw parse trees (`RawStmt` nodes). It intentionally stops before semantic analysis and rewriting.

---

### Why raw parsing is separated from analysis & rewriting

Analysis and rewriting **require access to system catalogs and database tables** and therefore **cannot run inside an aborted transaction**. PostgreSQL must still be able to recognize critical commands like `COMMIT` or `ABORT` even when the transaction is aborted, so the raw parser is used as a lightweight, table-free first stage. When the backend is in abort state, non-critical commands are halted after raw parsing; only `COMMIT`/`ABORT` (detected by the raw parser) are allowed through.

---

### Parsing delegation

```
pg_parse_query(query_string)               [src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:617]
    ↓
raw_parser(query_string, RAW_PARSE_DEFAULT) [src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:626; src/backend/parser/parser.c:42]
    ↓ initializes flex scanner (scanner_init) and bison parser (parser_init)
    ↓
base_yyparse(yyscanner)                    [src/backend/parser/parser.c:73]
    ↓ (generated bison parser from gram.y, using lexer from scan.l)
```

The raw parse trees returned by `base_yyparse` are then stored in `yyextra.parsetree` and returned up the chain.

`pg_parse_query` performs **raw parsing only** — lexical and grammatical analysis of a SQL query string, returning a `List` of raw parse trees (`RawStmt` nodes). It intentionally stops before semantic analysis and rewriting.

---

### Why raw parsing is separated from analysis & rewriting

Analysis and rewriting **require access to system catalogs and database tables** and therefore **cannot run inside an aborted transaction**. PostgreSQL must still be able to recognize critical commands like `COMMIT` or `ABORT` even when the transaction is aborted, so the raw parser is used as a lightweight, table-free first stage. When the backend is in abort state, non-critical commands are halted after raw parsing; only `COMMIT`/`ABORT` (detected by the raw parser) are allowed through.

---

### Parsing delegation

```
pg_parse_query(query_string)               [src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:617]
    ↓
raw_parser(query_string, RAW_PARSE_DEFAULT) [src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:626; src/backend/parser/parser.c:42]
    ↓ initializes flex scanner (scanner_init) and bison parser (parser_init)
    ↓
base_yyparse(yyscanner)                    [src/backend/parser/parser.c:73]
    ↓ (generated bison parser from gram.y, using lexer from scan.l)
```

The raw parse trees returned by `base_yyparse` are then stored in `yyextra.parsetree` and returned up the chain.

Analysis and rewriting **require access to system catalogs and database tables** and therefore **cannot run inside an aborted transaction**. `pg_parse_query` performs **raw parsing only** — lexical and grammatical analysis of a SQL query string, returning a `List` of raw parse trees (`RawStmt` nodes). It intentionally stops before semantic analysis and rewriting.

---

### Why raw parsing is separated from analysis & rewriting

Analysis and rewriting **require access to system catalogs and database tables** and therefore **cannot run inside an aborted transaction**. PostgreSQL must still be able to recognize critical commands like `COMMIT` or `ABORT` even when the transaction is aborted, so the raw parser is used as a lightweight, table-free first stage. When the backend is in abort state, non-critical commands are halted after raw parsing; only `COMMIT`/`ABORT` (detected by the raw parser) are allowed through.

---

pg_parse_query(query_string)               [src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:617]
    ↓
raw_parser(query_string, RAW_PARSE_DEFAULT) [src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:626; src/backend/parser/parser.c:42]
    ↓ initializes flex scanner (scanner_init) and bison parser (parser_init)
    ↓
base_yyparse(yyscanner)                    [src/backend/parser/parser.c:73]

`pg_parse_query` performs **raw parsing only** — lexical and grammatical analysis of a SQL query string, returning a `List` of raw parse trees (`RawStmt` nodes). It intentionally stops before semantic analysis and rewriting.

### Why raw parsing is separated from analysis & rewriting

Analysis and rewriting **require access to system catalogs and database tables** and therefore **cannot run inside an aborted transaction**. PostgreSQL must still be able to recognize critical commands like `COMMIT` or `ABORT` even when the transaction is aborted, so the raw parser is used as a lightweight, table-free first stage. When the backend is in abort state, non-critical commands are halted after raw parsing; only `COMMIT`/`ABORT` (detected by the raw parser) are allowed through.
